highlights.title: Release notes
highlights.description: New features for this release appear here when you ship a tag.

highlights.title: Release notes
highlights.description: Annotation Task Table now has spectogram preview on click or using arrow keys up and down. Bulk tag operations with shortscuts also implemented.

highlights.title: Release notes
highlights.description: Annotate View has full screen mode on press of Keyboard w. Selected Sound Event now has zoom and measure actions.

highlights.title: Guided user tour
highlights.description: Start a personal tutorial from the home page and follow the lessons step by step. Pick up where you left off, or start from scratch. Your copy is hidden from the annotation projects list.

highlights.title: Release notes
highlights.description: Multiple sound event selection and restructured Annotate View, Tag page and Tag Keyboard shortcuts.

highlights.title: Faster filters on large projects
highlights.description: Tag, tag amount, sound event amount, confidence and median confidence filters now finish within seconds, also on projects with more than 100 000 tasks. Tag filters are applied when you press Apply, and the task list shows “Filtering…” while new results load.

highlights.title: Sound event tags and task tags filtered separately
highlights.description: The “Sound event tags” filter looks only at the tags of sound events. A new “Task tags” filter covers tags on the task itself, with include/exclude, AND/OR and the number of distinct tags.

highlights.title: Tasks grouped by night
highlights.description: Switch the task table between List and Nights. Nights shows every night (noon to noon) collapsed with its status counts; expand a night to load its tasks. In List, a header row marks where a new night starts.

highlights.title: Reference calls
highlights.description: The tasks page can show up to 20 of the clearest, loudest calls of a species side by side, with their signal-to-noise ratio and peak level. Click a call to open its task, or pin the panel to keep it on the project's tasks page.

highlights.title: Main frequencies and PSD
highlights.description: A new panel in the Annotate view lists the median, min and max peak frequency of a task's calls per species and call type; click a call to select its sound event. The PSD of a sound event now uses a fixed 10–110 kHz axis with a 40 kHz mark, and is measured at the right time in tasks that do not start at 0 s.

highlights.title: Edit history and prediction corrections
highlights.description: The Annotate view shows the edit history of the sound events, including their original detector tags and confidence. The project overview shows how reviewers corrected the detector's predictions: confirmed, relabeled, tag removed or event deleted.

highlights.title: Bulk actions without a task limit
highlights.description: Bulk actions in the task table work on any number of tasks, with a progress bar and a Stop button. A new “Remove status” menu (Shift + 1–4) removes a status from the selected tasks.

highlights.title: Task table and Annotate view
highlights.description: Clicking a row or moving with the arrow keys selects that task, so the status keys 1–4 act on it; Shift + click or Shift + arrows select a range. In the Annotate view, Shift + d deletes the sound events whose only tag is the one you pick. Shift + U saves the current zoom as the default.

highlights.title: Annotate view opens faster
highlights.description: The Annotate view no longer waits for the task counts of the filter, and the Annotate tab opens the first task of the task table's filter right away.

highlights.title: Projects in folders
highlights.description: Filter the project list by detector and year, and file projects in folders: tick them or drag them onto a folder. Folders are kept in your browser.

highlights.title: Species overview
highlights.description: The species overview shows in how many tasks and recordings each species occurs.

highlights.title: Fixes
highlights.description: Replacing tags with a tag the sound event already has no longer leaves it untagged. While the next page of tasks loads, the previous page's tasks are no longer shown in its place. The Tags page loads quickly on large databases.
